Theme

face verb

lie towards a direction

also face north, face south, face east, face west, look out on, facing, face up to, confront, face danger, lie in the direction of, slope towards, facing south

classical

Caes. BG 1.1.6: Belgae spectant in septentriōnēs et orientem sōlem (Lewis & Short s.v. spectō)
Traupman 204
Caes. BG 5.13: alter angulus ad orientem sōlem … spectat (Lewis & Short s.v. alter)
Traupman 312

spectō, spectāre, spectāvī, spectātum

with in or ad + accusative

face, look towards (of places and peoples)

Other words

  • vergō, vergere — of a place: lie towards, face, slope towards

    verb, third conjugation, with ad or in + acc. · also used · classical · Caes. BG 1.1: Galliae pars ad septentriōnēs (Lewis & Short); Liv. 37.31.10: portus in merīdiem (Lewis & Short); Traupman 339

    Lewis & Short calls this the classical sense of the word: a place, a building or a slope “inclines” towards a quarter. Lewis & Short, after Neue, gives no perfect or supine.

  • obviam īre (+ dative) — face up to, confront (a danger); a different sense from facing a direction

    also used · classical · Sall. J. 7.4: obviam īre perīculīs, to meet dangers courageously (Lewis & Short s.v. obviam); Traupman 312

Examples

  • spectāre in (ad) septentriōnēs (merīdiem, orientem, occidentem)

    to face north (south, east, west)Traupman 312

See also north, south, east, west.

SourcesJohn C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, cited by printed page; each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
